t12-001.title: Handbook operating-system I/O, API, and capacity examples

entries.epoll: Linux readiness notification interface for monitoring file descriptors; applications still handle nonblocking state, edge/level-trigger semantics, and resource limits.
entries.kqueue: BSD-family kernel event notification interface for monitoring descriptor and other event filters; exact filters and semantics vary by operating system.
entries.io_uring: Linux asynchronous I/O interface using shared submission/completion rings; supported operations and performance depend on kernel version, driver, workload, and safe cancellation behavior.
entries.Filesystem internals: File-system metadata, journaling or copy-on-write behavior, page cache, durability barriers, and device behavior influence persistence and latency; names alone do not establish crash guarantees.
entries.Memory hierarchy: Registers, caches, RAM, and storage have different capacity and access costs; cache locality, working set, and page faults can dominate observed latency.
entries.Little's Law: For a stable system, average number of items in a system equals throughput multiplied by average time in the system; define the system boundary and consistent units before applying it.
entries.GraphQL N+1 query problem: Resolver execution can issue repeated backend reads for related fields; batching, data loaders, query planning, and bounded complexity can reduce amplification but must preserve authorization and caching semantics.
entries.gRPC streaming: gRPC supports unary and streaming RPC shapes; flow control, deadlines, cancellation, message size, and reconnect behavior are part of the application contract.
entries.Cursor pagination: Uses a stable continuation position rather than an offset; define sort order, tie-breaker, cursor integrity, concurrent changes, and authorization scope.
entries.API versioning and evolution: May use additive compatible changes, explicit versions, media types, or negotiated capabilities; deprecation and old-client support need telemetry and a removal policy.
entries.Idempotency key: A client-supplied operation identifier lets a server recognize retries for the same logical command; scope, retention, request equivalence, concurrency, and stored outcome must be defined.

t12-001.title: Handbook building-block products, protocols, and cache policies

entries.AWS Application Load Balancer (ALB): AWS-managed Layer 7 load-balancing service; compare its routing and health behavior with the chosen deployment and verify current service limits in AWS documentation.
entries.AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB): AWS-managed Layer 4 load-balancing service; compare connection and protocol needs, target behavior, and limits with ALB and other providers.
entries.Google Cloud Pub/Sub: Managed messaging and event delivery service; choose between its subscription and retention semantics and other brokers using current delivery, ordering, and quota documentation.
entries.Amazon SNS: AWS managed pub/sub notification service; fan-out, filtering, ordering, retries, and integration behavior depend on configuration and connected services.
entries.WebRTC: Real-time media/data communication technologies for browsers and applications; signaling, ICE, STUN/TURN, congestion control, and server topology remain system responsibilities.
entries.MQTT: Lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol commonly used for constrained devices; QoS levels, session behavior, broker persistence, and authorization need explicit selection.
entries.Google Cloud Storage (GCS): Managed object-storage service; verify consistency, access controls, lifecycle, retention, and request limits in current product documentation.
entries.MinIO: S3-compatible object-storage software; compatibility, deployment, erasure coding, and operational behavior depend on its version and configuration.
entries.Cloudflare Workers: Cloudflare edge-compute platform; runtime, state, CPU, networking, and product limits are platform-specific and change over time.
entries.AWS Lambda@Edge: AWS edge compute integrated with CloudFront events; supported runtimes, regions, event phases, and constraints must be checked in current AWS docs.
entries.Deno Deploy: Deno-based edge/serverless deployment platform named by the Handbook; confirm current product status, runtime, APIs, and limits in its official documentation.
entries.Cloudflare Durable Objects: Cloudflare stateful coordination primitive with object identity and location semantics; it is not a general globally distributed database and its consistency/limits must be checked in current docs.
entries.Edge database: A database deployed near edge workloads; define replication, conflict, ownership, data residency, offline behavior, and reconciliation instead of assuming edge locality implies global consistency.
entries.Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction: Evicts entries based on recency approximations; scan-heavy workloads and metadata overhead can make it a poor fit.
entries.TinyLFU eviction: Uses frequency-aware admission to resist cache pollution and can be combined with a recency policy; benchmark implementation and workload behavior.
entries.Cache stampede prevention: Coordinates or staggers refreshes so many misses do not simultaneously overload an origin; leases, jitter, stale serving, and single-flight have distinct failure behavior.
entries.APNs: Apple Push Notification service for delivering notifications to Apple devices; delivery is asynchronous and token lifecycle, throttling, and feedback behavior must be handled.
entries.Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM): Firebase messaging service for sending messages to supported clients; device token lifecycle, delivery outcomes, platform differences, and quotas need current documentation.

t12-002.title: Handbook consensus, quorum, failure-detection, and hashing algorithms

entries.Multi-Paxos: A consensus protocol optimized around a stable leader for repeated log decisions; distinguish its safety assumptions and implementation details from Raft.
entries.Read quorum and write quorum: Replica acknowledgement thresholds whose intersection can support particular consistency guarantees only under the protocol's failure, version, and replica assumptions.
entries.Sloppy quorum: Accepts writes on reachable substitute nodes when preferred replicas are unavailable; later handoff and reconciliation affect consistency and durability.
entries.Hinted handoff: Temporarily stores a replica's missed update at another node for later delivery; it is repair support, not by itself a consistency guarantee.
entries.G-Counter: A grow-only counter CRDT whose per-replica components merge by component-wise maximum; it supports increments but not decrement without a different construction.
entries.PN-Counter: A CRDT counter composed from positive and negative grow-only components to represent increments and decrements under its merge assumptions.
entries.Observed-Remove Set (OR-Set): A set CRDT that associates additions with unique tags so a remove targets observed additions; concurrent unseen adds can remain after a remove.
entries.Last-Write-Wins Register (LWW-Register): Selects a value by timestamp and tie-break rule; clock skew and concurrent user intent can cause one update to be discarded.
entries.SWIM membership protocol: A scalable membership and failure-detection protocol based on randomized probing and gossip; suspicion is evidence, not proof that a node failed.
entries.Phi accrual failure detector: Converts heartbeat arrival history into a suspicion level rather than a binary timeout; tune thresholds to workload and network behavior.
entries.Bounded-load consistent hashing: Consistent hashing variant that caps node load and may redirect keys when a target is full; capacity, imbalance, and remapping effects need evaluation.
entries.Maglev hashing: Consistent hashing construction designed for fast lookup and limited remapping as backend membership changes; table size and health behavior affect operations.
entries.Jump consistent hash: Compact algorithm mapping keys to buckets with low remapping when bucket count changes; its bucket model differs from weighted heterogeneous nodes.
entries.Read repair: Repairs divergent replicas during reads in some storage systems; it can add read latency and does not replace anti-entropy or a stated consistency model.

t12-003.title: Handbook storage engines, lakehouse formats, and data-platform examples

entries.InnoDB: MySQL's default general-purpose storage engine in current common distributions; inspect transaction, locking, indexing, and durability behavior for the deployed version.
entries.Delta Lake: Open table format and transaction-log layer for data lakes; protocol features, concurrency, and engine compatibility are version-dependent.
entries.Apache Iceberg: Open table format for large analytic datasets; catalog, snapshot, schema evolution, and engine support are defined by specification and implementation versions.
entries.Apache Hudi: Data lake table/data-management framework supporting incremental and transactional table operations; choose table type and query engine based on its documented guarantees.
entries.Apache Hadoop: Distributed storage and processing ecosystem; Hadoop Distributed File System and MapReduce are distinct components with different operational roles.
entries.Kafka Streams: Java library for building stream-processing applications using Kafka topics and state stores; processing and delivery guarantees depend on topology and configuration.
entries.Spark Structured Streaming: Spark's stream-processing engine using DataFrame/Dataset APIs; trigger, source/sink, checkpoint, and end-to-end semantics depend on the connector and query.
entries.Maxwell's Daemon: MySQL binlog-based change-data-capture tool named by the Handbook; verify supported versions, output semantics, and recovery behavior in its project documentation.
entries.Apache Solr: Distributed search platform based on Lucene; schema, indexing, query, and cluster behavior should be compared with Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for the workload.
entries.Amazon Neptune: Managed graph database service supporting documented graph models and APIs; verify engine-specific transaction, query, and topology support in AWS docs.
entries.Dgraph: Distributed graph database named by the Handbook; product status, licensing, API, and current deployment model require confirmation from the project's current official sources.
entries.Thanos: Components that extend Prometheus-compatible metrics storage with long-term retention and global querying; deployment topology and consistency depend on selected components.
entries.Cortex: Horizontally scalable, multi-tenant Prometheus metrics system named by the Handbook; check its current project status and operational architecture before selection.

t12-004.title: Handbook architecture patterns, operations, and security examples

entries.Conway's Law: Organizational communication structures tend to shape system designs; treat this as a design observation, not a deterministic law that dictates a specific architecture.
entries.Notification, state-transfer, and domain: Different event purposes have different coupling and replay implications; name whether a message announces a fact, carries state, or requests work.
entries.Choreography: Participants react to events without a central workflow coordinator; observability, cycle control, and global process visibility need deliberate design.
entries.AWS Lambda: AWS event-driven function compute; concurrency, timeout, cold-start, retry, and delivery semantics depend on trigger and configuration.
entries.Google Cloud Functions: Google-managed event-driven function compute; current product naming, runtime, regions, and limits should be verified in Google Cloud documentation.
entries.Azure Functions: Azure event-driven function compute; hosting plan, trigger, scaling, execution, and retry behavior vary by plan and configuration.
entries.Clean Architecture: Dependency-direction approach that places policy inward from delivery and infrastructure details; naming a layer does not guarantee a useful boundary.
entries.Onion Architecture: Layering approach that keeps domain policy central and dependencies directed inward; adapt boundaries to actual change and testing needs.
entries.Yjs: CRDT framework for collaborative applications named by the Handbook; provider, persistence, awareness, and conflict semantics need current project documentation.
entries.Automerge: CRDT-based data and sync framework named by the Handbook; inspect its current data model, sync protocol, storage, and versioned APIs.
entries.Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA): Kubernetes controller that adjusts replica counts from configured metrics; it does not provision cluster capacity and responds with metric/control-loop delay.
entries.Cluster Autoscaler: Kubernetes component that adjusts node groups to fit pending pods; provider integration, scale-up delay, and consolidation behavior vary.
entries.Predictive autoscaling: Forecasts demand to provision capacity before expected load; forecast error, warm-up time, cost, and fallback reactive capacity matter.
entries.LaunchDarkly: Commercial feature-management platform named by the Handbook; SDK behavior, evaluation, streaming, and service limits are product/version specific.
entries.Chaos Monkey: Netflix-originated failure-injection tool/example; chaos experiments require scoped hypotheses, safety controls, and observed recovery, not random production breakage.
entries.Fault injection game day: A planned resilience exercise that introduces a bounded failure and measures detection, containment, recovery, and user impact.
entries.Backstage: Open-source developer portal framework named by the Handbook; plugins, catalog ownership, authorization, and operations need current project documentation.
entries.DORA metrics: Measures related to software delivery performance; use current definitions and avoid optimizing a metric in isolation from reliability and user outcomes.
entries.SPACE framework: Developer productivity measurement framework spanning satisfaction, performance, activity, communication/collaboration, and efficiency/flow; it cautions against reducing productivity to one metric.
entries.Spot instances: Interruptible discounted compute capacity; workloads need interruption handling, checkpointing, and capacity fallback.
entries.Reserved capacity: Provider-specific commitment or reservation that can reduce unit cost under utilization assumptions; compare term, scope, flexibility, and opportunity cost.
entries.Cost unit economics: Relates cost to a useful product unit such as successful request, tenant, transaction, or model answer; define quality and workload so lower cost does not merely mean less service.

t12-004.title: Handbook security identity, compliance, supply-chain, and cryptography examples

entries.SpiceDB: Authorization database built around relationship-based access control, named by the Handbook; verify schema, consistency, and operational behavior in current official docs.
entries.OpenFGA: Open-source authorization system inspired by Zanzibar-style relationship tuples, named by the Handbook; evaluate model expressiveness, consistency, and deployment requirements.
entries.AWS IAM: AWS identity and access management service and policy system; effective permissions combine identity, resource, organization, and other policy controls.
entries.OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE: Delegated authorization flow using a code verifier/challenge to protect public clients; validate redirect URI, state, issuer, token audience, and current security best practice.
entries.OpenID Connect (OIDC): Identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 that defines authentication and ID tokens; validate issuer, audience, signature, nonce, and flow-specific requirements.
entries.JWS: JSON Web Signature representation for integrity/authenticity protection; it does not encrypt the payload.
entries.JWE: JSON Web Encryption representation for confidentiality protection; encryption alone does not establish trusted issuer identity.
entries.SPIFFE: Specification for workload identity documents and trust domains; deployment requires a trust bundle and identity issuance policy.
entries.SPIRE: Implementation of SPIFFE workload identity issuance and attestation; agent/server topology and selectors determine workload identity.
entries.HashiCorp Vault: Secrets and cryptographic services platform named by the Handbook; current licensing, auth methods, storage, and feature support should be checked in official docs.
entries.AWS Secrets Manager: Managed secret storage and rotation service; rotation support and lifecycle differ by secret type and integration.
entries.Key Management Service (KMS): Cloud key-management service for cryptographic keys and envelope-encryption workflows; key policies, regional scope, and service limits matter.
entries.AWS Shield: AWS DDoS protection service family; protection tier, covered resources, and response features are provider-specific.
entries.GDPR: EU data-protection regulation; applicability, lawful basis, data-subject rights, transfers, and controller/processor duties require jurisdiction-specific legal analysis.
entries.Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DP: India's personal data protection statute; applicability and current implementing rules must be checked against official Indian legal sources.
entries.California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA/CP: California privacy-law framework as amended by CPRA; applicability and duties depend on current law, regulations, and facts.
entries.LGPD: Brazilian General Data Protection Law; determine territorial scope, legal basis, rights, and obligations from current official sources.
entries.Cryptographic erasure (crypto-shredding): Makes encrypted data inaccessible by destroying or revoking relevant keys; shared keys, replicas, logs, backups, and key recovery complicate proof of deletion.
entries.SLSA provenance: Supply-chain framework for describing build provenance and assurance levels; level requirements and implementation status must follow the current specification.
entries.Sigstore: Open-source signing and verification ecosystem for software artifacts; identity, transparency log, keyless signing, and verifier policy need explicit configuration.
entries.xz-utils compromise: Supply-chain incident involving malicious code introduced into xz-utils releases; use it as a case for provenance, maintainer trust, and dependency monitoring, not as a generic signature failure.
entries.SolarWinds Orion compromise: Supply-chain incident involving a compromised software build and downstream distribution; response needs provenance, build isolation, and detection beyond dependency version pinning.
entries.Secure aggregation: Cryptographic protocol family that limits what an aggregator learns from individual participants' contributions; dropout, collusion, and implementation assumptions matter.
entries.Homomorphic encryption: Cryptographic techniques enabling selected computations over ciphertext; supported operations, performance, and key management limit practical use.
entries.ML-KEM: NIST-standardized key-encapsulation mechanism in FIPS 203 (published 2024); NIST currently lists potential errata, so check the current publication and errata before protocol integration or hybrid migration.
entries.ML-DSA: NIST-standardized digital-signature scheme in FIPS 204 (published 2024); NIST currently lists potential errata, so check the current publication and errata before selecting parameter sets or deployment guidance.

t12-006.title: Handbook case-study-specific algorithms, protocols, and product techniques

entries.Redis Lua atomic operation: Runs a server-side script atomically relative to other Redis commands, subject to Redis execution and script constraints; it is not a multi-system transaction.
entries.Two-tier local and global rate limit: Combines cheap local admission with a shared global policy; local bursts, synchronization delay, and failure mode determine how closely the global limit is enforced.
entries.Dead-letter queue: Stores messages that exceed a delivery policy for inspection or later replay; it needs bounded retention, ownership, alerting, and safe redrive procedures.
entries.End-to-end encryption (E2EE): Encrypts content so intermediary services cannot ordinarily read plaintext; key verification, metadata exposure, multi-device history, and recovery remain design questions.
entries.Celebrity fan-out problem: A highly followed account creates disproportionate feed fan-out; hybrid push/pull and bounded read-time merging trade write work against read latency.
entries.Origin shielding for CDN: Uses an intermediate cache layer to reduce duplicate origin fetches; cache key, purge, stale, and regional-failure behavior must preserve content correctness.
entries.Robots Exclusion Protocol (robots.txt): A crawler convention defined by RFC 9309 for crawler access rules; it is not access control and does not guarantee that a site is private.
entries.Top-K precomputation: Precomputes popular suggestions or rankings to reduce request-time work; freshness, personalization, and long-tail fallback need explicit handling.
entries.HLS: HTTP Live Streaming protocol family for media delivery; playlist, segment, encryption, and low-latency features vary by version and implementation.
entries.MPEG-DASH: Adaptive-bitrate streaming standard using media presentation descriptions and segments; player, codec, DRM, and packaging compatibility must be tested.
entries.CMAF: Common Media Application Format for fragmented media segments that can support interoperable streaming workflows; codec and packaging profiles still matter.
entries.ISP peering: Network interconnection arrangement that can affect content-delivery paths and cost; routing and commercial agreements are outside application-level guarantees.
entries.Open Connect: Netflix's content delivery network program named in the Handbook; its deployment specifics are provider-operated and should not be assumed available to other services.
entries.Contraction hierarchies: Road-network routing preprocessing technique that accelerates shortest-path queries by adding shortcuts; preprocessing and update cost matter when the graph changes.
entries.Operational Transformation (OT): Collaborative-editing technique that transforms concurrent operations to preserve intended effects under a defined operation model; it is not interchangeable with every CRDT.
entries.Redis SETNX: Redis command that sets a key only if it does not already exist; lease expiry, clock/fencing, crash recovery, and atomic state transition remain important for locks.
entries.Virtual waiting room: Admission-control queue that regulates entry during demand spikes; fairness, abandonment, token integrity, and bypass prevention matter.
entries.Double-entry ledger: Accounting model where each transaction records balanced debit and credit entries; immutability, correction entries, currency precision, and reconciliation preserve auditability.
entries.FIFO order book: Matches compatible orders in arrival order within the same price level under a specified exchange rule; exchange-specific priorities and market regulations govern actual behavior.
entries.Price-time priority: Ranks executable orders first by price and then by time under a defined market rule; special order types and venue rules can alter matching.
entries.Downsampling: Reduces time-series resolution to control long-term storage and query cost; aggregation can discard spikes and must match the retained analytical purpose.
entries.Ad-click event-time windows: Aggregates clicks by event timestamp rather than arrival time; allowed lateness, correction, deduplication, and settlement finality must be explicit.
entries.Time-warp/reconciliation for file sync: Compares version vectors, block manifests, or content hashes to detect divergent edits and transfer only changed content; conflict policy and deletion tombstones must be retained.
entries.Redis GEO commands/geosets: Redis geospatial commands index coordinates for nearby searches; radius semantics, result scale, precision, and shard behavior require product-specific validation.
entries.H3 geospatial grid: Hierarchical global hexagonal indexing system with pentagonal cells; resolution and neighbor traversal affect aggregation and spatial joins.
entries.Temporal workflow orchestration: Durable workflow engine pattern that records workflow history and schedules activities; determinism, replay compatibility, task retries, and external side-effect idempotency must be handled.
entries.SSE token streaming: Streams generated text updates over Server-Sent Events; reconnect, event IDs, proxy buffering, authorization, and cancellation must be tested end to end.
entries.Firecracker microVM: Lightweight virtual-machine monitor used for workload isolation; a secure deployment still needs kernel, host, networking, image, and resource controls.
entries.seccomp: Linux facility for restricting a process's system calls; filter policy must match required syscalls and is one layer of sandboxing.
entries.Linux cgroups: Kernel mechanism for organizing and limiting resource use by process groups; controller availability and hierarchy depend on kernel and cgroup version.
entries.Software similarity plagiarism detection: Compares program structure or token similarity to flag possible copying; similarity is evidence for human review, not proof of misconduct.
entries.OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP): Protocol for transporting telemetry data to collectors/backends; signal version, semantic conventions, batching, retry, and cardinality affect operation.
entries.BM25 plus PageRank search ranking: Combines lexical relevance with a link-based importance signal; normalization, freshness, spam resistance, and evaluation determine whether the combination helps.
entries.Neural reranking cascade: Applies progressively more expensive rankers to a candidate set; each stage needs latency budget and relevance evaluation.
entries.SMTP ingress: Accepts or relays email using SMTP; authentication, queueing, abuse controls, TLS policy, bounce handling, and mail-domain reputation affect delivery.
entries.RFC 5322 message format: Internet Message Format syntax for message headers and bodies; MIME extensions and transport behavior are separate specifications.
entries.Content-addressed attachment deduplicati: Identifies identical content by a cryptographic digest to reduce duplicate storage; tenant privacy, hash disclosure, collision policy, and encryption scope matter.
entries.SFU: Selective Forwarding Unit routes received media streams to participants without mixing every stream into one output; bandwidth and topology shape client load.
entries.MCU: Multipoint Control Unit combines media streams into composed output; server compute and encode costs trade against client bandwidth and capability.
entries.Simulcast: Sends multiple encoded quality layers so a receiver or SFU can choose a suitable layer; extra upstream bandwidth and encoder cost are tradeoffs.
entries.Scalable Video Coding (SVC): Encodes a base layer with enhancement layers that can be selectively forwarded; codec, device, and network support must be verified.
entries.WebRTC STUN and TURN: STUN helps discover network address mappings; TURN relays traffic when direct connectivity fails, adding relay capacity, latency, and cost.
entries.Redis Lua compare-and-set bid: Checks and updates auction state atomically within Redis script execution; ensure bid ordering, idempotency, durability, and authoritative settlement rules.
entries.Delta-batched comment fan-out: Groups updates to reduce per-event fan-out overhead; batching adds delay and needs ordering, drop, and moderation semantics.
entries.Graph ring detection: Uses relationship-graph signals to identify cyclic or coordinated patterns; graph evidence is probabilistic and requires privacy and false-positive controls.
entries.Dynamic Time Warping (DTW): Measures similarity between sequences allowing nonlinear time alignment; windowing, normalization, and compute cost matter for large-scale matching.
entries.MOSS: Measure Of Software Similarity, a tool family named in the Handbook; similarity scores require context and human adjudication.
entries.Anycast DNS: Advertises the same IP prefix from multiple locations so routing sends clients to a nearby reachable site; routing convergence and health withdrawal need operational design.
entries.DNS over TLS (DoT): Carries DNS queries over TLS; endpoint identity, resolver policy, and port/network constraints matter.
entries.DNS over HTTPS (DoH): Carries DNS messages over HTTPS; endpoint choice and application/browser policy determine privacy and network observability.
entries.DNS over QUIC (DoQ): Carries DNS over QUIC; resolver support and connection behavior depend on current RFC and implementation versions.
entries.DNSSEC validation: Verifies DNS data signatures along a chain of trust; it authenticates DNS data origin/integrity, not confidentiality or the truth of the record.
entries.API Gateway at scale: Combines routing, authentication integration, quotas, TLS, and policy at a traffic boundary; keep business ownership, failure isolation, and control-plane rollout explicit.
entries.Content-addressed build artifact: Identifies an artifact by digest so cache reuse and integrity checks can be repeatable; provenance and access controls are separate requirements.
entries.Ephemeral CI runner: Short-lived worker for a build job; isolation, image provenance, credential scope, cleanup, and hostile workload controls must be enforced.
entries.Trace-log correlation: Links logs and trace spans through propagated context identifiers; avoid exposing secrets or high-cardinality personal identifiers in telemetry.
entries.Regulatory audit trail: Retains evidence of sensitive business actions and decisions with integrity and access controls; retention and deletion duties must be reconciled.
entries.EVCache: Netflix distributed in-memory cache system named by the Handbook; treat its architecture as a case-study example, not a generally available product choice.
entries.Bipartite matching for dispatch: Assigns workers and tasks across two sets using an optimization objective; online constraints, travel time, fairness, and changing availability make exact global matching costly.
entries.Surge pricing: Adjusts price or incentives in response to supply/demand conditions; define policy, fairness, transparency, regulatory, and feedback constraints.
entries.Map tile rendering: Precomputes or renders geographic map tiles at zoom levels; cache keys, projection, updates, and licensing affect serving and storage.
entries.Graph Neural Network (GNN) ETA predictio: Uses graph structure and learned signals for estimated arrival times; training data, calibration, drift, and safety constraints need evaluation.
entries.Offline maps: Stores map data for disconnected use; versioning, regional updates, storage limits, and routing freshness must be explicit.
entries.Block-level deduplication: Detects identical file chunks to reduce transfer or storage; chunk boundaries, hashes, privacy leakage, and encryption scope affect results.
entries.Delta sync: Transfers only changed data between client and server; version bases, concurrent writes, tombstones, and compaction require defined reconciliation.
entries.Presence broadcasting: Distributes short-lived information about active collaborators; high fan-out, expiry, privacy, and lossy delivery are usually handled separately from durable edits.
entries.Collaborative version history: Persists checkpoints or operations for recovery and audit; compaction, authorization, conflict handling, and retention affect storage and semantics.
entries.Collaborative filtering: Recommends from user-item interaction patterns; sparsity, feedback bias, privacy, and cold-start limitations need alternatives.
entries.Content-based recommendation: Uses item and user attributes to recommend similar content; feature quality, diversity, and filter bubbles should be measured.
entries.Anti-bot defenses: Combines abuse signals, risk-based challenges, rate controls, and review; avoid treating any single fingerprint or challenge as proof of automation.
entries.FIFO matching engine: Processes orders in a deterministic queue under explicit price-level and venue rules; persistence, replay, and regulatory audit are critical.
entries.Multicast market-data distribution: Publishes one feed to many subscribers over multicast-capable networks; packet loss recovery, sequencing, network support, and client entitlement are separate concerns.
entries.Colocation in trading systems: Places systems near exchange infrastructure to reduce network distance; it affects latency and cost but does not remove matching or correctness obligations.
entries.Approximate leaderboard rank: Trades exact global ordering for bounded computation or estimation for some views; disclose error and keep authoritative scores separate.
entries.Snowflake-style distributed IDs: Combines time and worker/sequence fields to generate IDs without one central counter; clock rollback, worker allocation, and bit layout affect uniqueness and ordering.
entries.ULID: 128-bit identifier format with a time component and randomness that is lexicographically sortable under its format; monotonic generation and collision risk depend on implementation.
entries.TSID: Time-sortable identifier family named by the Handbook; confirm the exact scheme and specification because the acronym is used for multiple designs.
entries.UUIDv7: Time-ordered UUID format standardized in RFC 9562; timestamp exposure, randomness, monotonic generation, and database ordering remain design considerations.
entries.PostgreSQL exclusion constraint for rese: Exclusion constraints can reject overlapping ranges for a defined key/operator combination; extension, isolation, and schema design must be checked for the actual database version.
entries.Exactly-once workflow execution claim: A workflow engine may provide durable orchestration and replay, but external side effects still require idempotency, deduplication, or reconciliation; avoid equating retries with exactly-once effects.
entries.OpenRouter: Model/API routing service named by the Handbook; inspect current provider routing, data handling, availability, pricing, and supported features before use.
entries.LiteLLM: Open-source proxy and SDK for a normalized interface across model providers; provider feature differences, routing, credentials, and compatibility need current documentation.
entries.Harness Feature Management & Experimenta: Feature-management and experimentation product named by the Handbook; verify current product naming, SDK behavior, and service limits in official docs.
entries.Unleash: Feature-flag and experimentation platform named by the Handbook; evaluate SDK evaluation, activation strategies, hosting, and current version behavior.
entries.Public recursive DNS over UDP and TCP: DNS query transport over UDP or TCP; response size, truncation fallback, amplification controls, and implementation support must be handled.
entries.Virtual private network (VPN) and encryp: Encrypted DNS protects the resolver link but changes network visibility and policy enforcement; distinguish DoT, DoH, DoQ, and ordinary DNS threat models.
entries.Mutual-match detection: Checks whether two users independently satisfy a matching rule; concurrency, privacy, abuse, and idempotent notification delivery need definition.
entries.Proxy bidding: Stores a bidder's maximum and automatically places bids according to auction rules; fairness, secrecy, tie-breaking, and atomic ordering are essential.
entries.Auction sniping extension: Extends closing time after a late bid under a published rule; race conditions, clock authority, and client-visible countdown must be specified.
entries.Peer-to-peer (P2P) media topology: Participants exchange media directly where network conditions allow; NAT traversal, participant count, moderation, and fallback relay behavior limit applicability.
entries.Bandwidth estimation for conferencing: Estimates usable path capacity to adapt media bitrate and layers; feedback delay, congestion, fairness, and loss concealment affect quality.
entries.Regional media routing: Places or forwards conference media through regional infrastructure to reduce path latency; migration, participant locality, encryption, and failover must be considered.
entries.Spam classification cascade: Applies successive rules and models to filter abuse at different cost/latency levels; false positives, appeals, and adversarial adaptation need review.
entries.Per-user sharded email search: Partitions search indexes by user or mailbox ownership; query scope, cross-user search, rebalancing, and hot accounts affect scaling.
entries.Tax-lot accounting: Tracks acquisition lots for securities and disposals; precision, corrections, jurisdictional rules, and auditability require authoritative records.
entries.Symbol-channel quote fan-out: Publishes market updates to subscribers by instrument/channel; hot symbols, sequencing, entitlement, and burst control shape the design.
entries.Priority-driven web scraping: Schedules crawler work by expected value and freshness; robots rules, source terms, rate limits, and politeness govern allowed behavior.
entries.Proxy-pool rotation: Routes requests through multiple egress addresses; rotation does not authorize access or bypass a site's terms and abuse controls.
entries.Diff-based price alert: Detects meaningful changes against prior observations and alerts subscribers; normalize prices, currency, availability, and noisy fluctuations.
entries.Hitless configuration reload: Applies routing or service configuration without dropping active traffic when the implementation supports it; validation, atomic rollout, and rollback still matter.
entries.YAML workflow DAG: Represents build jobs and dependencies as a directed acyclic graph; parser safety, expression evaluation, concurrency, and untrusted workflow isolation are essential.
entries.Dependency cache in CI: Reuses downloaded or compiled dependencies to reduce build time; key correctness, trust, invalidation, and poisoning risks need controls.
entries.Build secrets injection: Provides scoped credentials to isolated build steps; minimize lifetime and exposure, and prevent untrusted pull requests from accessing privileged secrets.
entries.Cardinality control for observability: Limits unbounded label dimensions to protect metrics storage and query cost; preserve useful diagnostic context through traces/logs with access controls.
entries.Fractional-share aggregation: Aggregates or records fractional ownership and orders according to brokerage rules; ledger, rounding, custody, and regulatory treatment must be explicit.

t12-006.title: Handbook system-design interview frameworks and tools

entries.RESHADED framework: Eight named steps: Requirements, Estimation, Storage schema (optional), High-level design, API design, Detailed design, Evaluation, and Distinctive component/feature. Use as a memory aid and time-box adaptively; its name does not replace requirements judgment.
entries.PEDALS framework: Six named steps: Process requirements, Estimate (optional), Design the service, Articulate the data model, List architectural components, and Scale. It is a checklist; add explicit tradeoff communication and a wrap-up when your interview rubric needs them.
entries.ADEPT framework: A community-derived sequence: Ask clarifying questions, Define requirements, Estimate, Propose design, and Tune with trade-offs. It is not a single canonical standard; use the letters as a prompt, not as evidence of an official company rubric.
entries.Alex Xu four-step framework: Understand problem/scope, propose a high-level design, deep-dive, and wrap up; add explicit API/data-model work when the prompt and interviewer need it.
entries.Hello Interview Delivery Framework: A delivery framework that emphasizes requirements, core entities, interface/API, high-level design, and deep dives with adaptable time budgets; skip estimation only when the calculation will not change the design.
entries.Grokking six-step framework: A time-boxed sequence of clarification, estimation, APIs, high-level design, deep dive, and scale/tradeoffs; adjust timings to the actual interview length and keep enough time for depth.
entries.interviewing.io three-step framework: A concise structure of requirements, data types/API/scale, and design; its brevity helps recall but the candidate must still cover failure, tradeoffs, and a clear conclusion.
entries.MoSCoW prioritization: A requirements prioritization technique grouping Must, Should, Could, and Won't (for this time/release); agree the meaning and scope of each category with stakeholders.
entries.Excalidraw: Collaborative whiteboard/diagramming tool named by the Handbook; tool familiarity and access matter, while diagram clarity and decision reasoning matter more than visual polish.
entries.Miro: Collaborative online whiteboard named by the Handbook; confirm the interview environment's allowed tool and collaboration setup in advance.
entries.Company-specific interview prompts: The Handbook names Amazon, Google, Meta, and Netflix as examples; do not assume fixed company rubrics from anecdotes, and prioritize the role, prompt, interviewer guidance, and current official recruiting material.
entries.Design RFC and Architecture Decision Rec: An RFC/design proposal invites review of context, options, consequences, and implementation; an ADR records one decision and rationale. Team conventions define exact format, ownership, and approval process.
